provenance.membership_note: Curated US theme baskets for monitoring rotation. Descriptive only, not a buy list.
provenance.membership_history_note: Available history comes from the S&P 1500 and baskets-only price caches. Basket levels are BACK-PROJECTED: a basket curated after seed_date is charted with its current roster carried backward over that roster's own price history, so the line shows what today's members did in the past, not what anyone held at the time. 35 of the 49 baskets here are back-projected this way. Membership changes are recorded per basket in `changelog`, and each member carries its true curation date in `curated_added` (see `added_semantics`) — treat the history before a member's `curated_added` as context, never as a track record.
provenance.membership_added_semantics: Each member carries TWO dates and they mean different things. `added` is the index-inclusion mask: the first date this member's price counts toward the basket's equal-weight level, back-projected to seed_date for any roster curated later, and it is what engine/baskets.py and its sibling engines read. `curated_added` is the provenance stamp: the date a curator actually put this name in this basket, never earlier than the basket's own `created`. Read `curated_added` — never `added` — when asking how long a name has been watched, or whether a signal predates its curation.

deviations: SPY is NOT in the ohlcv price root; benchmark read from /Users/chriswong/actions-runner-2/_work/macro/macro/data/yahoo/SPY.parquet (charter §2 named the ohlcv root).

C1 AS SHIPPED IS 'C1-RELAXED', NOT THE CHARTER-LITERAL LANE. Charter §1 orders C1's legs — 3D washout cross FIRST, then 'CONFIRMED by the first 1D MACD-RSI bull cross ... within the next 10 sessions'. The commissioning spec added an IMMEDIATE branch (fire at the 3D knowability date K when 1D macd >= sig at K AND the last 1D cross-up was within the prior 5 sessions), which admits a 1D cross already IN FORCE before the 3D leg — the opposite leg order. That branch carries 5926 of C1's 7973 panel episodes (74%), so C1's headline numbers are mostly not the charter's construction. Implemented as specified; the charter-literal lane is measured beside it as C1L in R9b.

C4's oversold qualifier is evaluated at the CONFIRM session p+3, not at the pivot p. Charter §1 says the pivot must print 'while the last completed 3D StochRSI %D < 20'; the commissioning spec pinned '%D < 20 as of p+3'. The p+3 reading is the knowability-conservative one (at p the p+3 confirm does not yet exist, and a %D read at p can still be revised by the bucket that closes between p and p+3), but it is a different test from the charter's wording and can admit a pivot whose oversold context arrived only after the pivot printed.

HL 2026-07-31 structure stop does NOT reproduce on the FULL-history recompute (charter §4 named it as a must-appear receipt). It DOES reproduce at other leading-history phases (R4.hl_phase). Cause: charting-app confluence_v2._arm_event_daily still cuts its 2B/3B bars with pandas `resample`, whose bin edges are phased to the SERIES' FIRST timestamp — the served slice and the full history are different grids. Both readings printed; nothing tuned.

§8 2x2 axis: the charter says 'the single strongest LIVE feature'. The strongest by raw spread is label-COUPLED (f_dist_swing) — its cells differ by how far stop A sits from the entry BY CONSTRUCTION, so cross-tabbing it would measure the ruler, not foresight. The 2x2 uses the strongest NON-coupled feature instead; the coupled row is still printed in full in the ledger with its spread and CI.

BREADTH LANE IS TIME-BOUNDED: membership `added` is the index-inclusion mask back-projected to seed_date=2023-05-09, and 986 of 1038 memberships carry exactly that date. Honouring it point-in-time means NO episode before 2023-05-09 has a live roster, so §3 and the §8 breadth features are measured only on the post-2023-05-09 slice of each lane (episode counts in R3/R8 show the shortfall). This is a substrate limit, not a null result.

R9c.title: Repeat-fire flag — point-in-time audit (was the prior fire's false start OBSERVABLE at T?)
R9c.notes: the shipped flag asks whether a prior fire's episode WAS a false start, a label built from windows extending past T; the PIT flag asks only whether its stop-A touch had already printed by T. The leaked subset scoring ~100% false-start is STRUCTURAL, not a discovery: a prior fire whose stop-A touch prints only after T breaks a low that sits inside the current episode's own [T-45, T] window too, so the same breach stops the current fire. That is the look-ahead, stated as an identity.

R9i.title: Pre-trough vs post-trough fires, per lane
R9i.notes: td_to_trough < 0 = fired BEFORE the eventual trough (the knife is still falling); >= 0 = fired after it. The post-trough false-bounce column is 0 BY IDENTITY: if the two-sided argmin low over [T-45, T+15] lands at or before T, no forward low in (T, T+15] can undercut it, so the false-bounce test cannot fire. `false_bounce` is therefore very nearly a restatement of `td_to_trough < 0`, and every §8 feature that separates false starts is to that extent separating pre-trough fires from post-trough ones.
